claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this, I need to gather some information about your situation and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under 16 years old, or children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - Alex, who is 17 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17 and living with you, I need to ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, are they attending school, college, university, or doing an approved apprenticeship or training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They finished school but haven't started anything new yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex is 17 and no longer in approved education or training, I need to ask:

**Has Alex registered with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with a careers service or the armed forces. They just left school and haven't signed up for anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask one more important question:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me now assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 17 years old
- Alex is not in approved education or training
- Alex has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- You live in the UK and Alex lives with you

According to the Child Benefit rules, you can normally continue to receive Child Benefit for a child aged 16 or over if they remain in approved education or training. Additionally, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

Since Alex is 17, no longer in approved education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services, you would not qualify for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

However, if Alex were to register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, you could claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from the date they left education or training.

conversation.text: I hope this has clarified your situation. If you have any other questions or if Alex's circumstances change, please let me know.
